replies.author: incompetentanddumb
replies.body:
I had to rewatch some of the scenes 2 or even 3 times to really understand what is going on because the visual feedback is very rough. What i mostly mean are the animations. Some of them are really fast and don't give you that much time to really process what is happening. After watching the trailer a few times i have a better understanding of whats going on but the first time i was very confused because the entire thing didn't feel that clear and coherent. 

To make the feedback a little less abstract lets go with the scene at 0:20 he says "Say hello to Kevin" holding a gray "something" in his hand. Then a mouse spawns and runs away. It stops randomly for a frame and the next scene happens. During the first watch i had barely any time to process what was happening here. I didn't notice gav was holding something and to me it looked like a mouse spawned out of nowhere. I genuinely did not have the time to connect the dots and to make sense out of the scene. This is problematic because i also had this issue with other scenes and they happen quickly after another, so while you are processing what just happened in one scene, there is already more going in the next.

I think the animations need less room for interpretation. You need to be able to understand what the objects of interest are without much cognitive effort. Also give the viewer a bit more time to understand whats happening, maybe?
